original_question:
Design a digital circuit in Verilog that functions as an active-low 3-to-8 decoder. The circuit should take a 3-bit input and activate (set to low) exactly one of its 8 output lines corresponding to the decimal value of the input. All other output lines should be inactive (set to high).

Your Verilog module must be named `decoder_3to8`.
It should have the following inputs:
- `A` (Most Significant Bit of the 3-bit input)
- `B` (Middle Bit of the 3-bit input)
- `C` (Least Significant Bit of the 3-bit input)

It should have the following outputs:
- `Y0`
- `Y1`
- `Y2`
- `Y3`
- `Y4`
- `Y5`
- `Y6`
- `Y7`

Implement the logic such that when the input `ABC` (where A is MSB, C is LSB) has the decimal value `i` (from 0 to 7), the output `Yi` is 0 and all other `Yj` (j != i) are 1.
